title: Lesson Plan — A Bottle of Dew (Class 6 CBSE English)
subject: English
objectives: Identify the main characters, setting and key events of the story.
Retell the story in 4-6 sentences using your own words.
Use key vocabulary (precious, thankful, delicately, balanced, dew, courtyard) correctly in sentences.
Explain why each character brought the offering they did.
State and justify the moral of the story.
Identify common nouns, proper nouns, adjectives, and past-tense verbs in given sentences.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the idea of a story / fable.
Basic understanding of nouns and verbs from earlier classes.
materials: Photocopies of the story (one per student)
Cards labelled with vocabulary words and meanings for a matching game
Cards with sentences for noun / adjective / past-tense identification

activities.description: Hook with a question: 'If a king asked you to bring the most precious thing in the world, what would you bring?' Take 3-4 student responses; tally them on the board. Promise the story will reveal what one wise child brought.
teacher_actions: Write each idea on the board.
Promise the answer in the reading.

activities.description: Read the story aloud (or have students read in pairs). After reading, students write down (in two minutes) which character's offering surprised them most and why.
teacher_actions: Read with feeling, especially the child's lines.
Pause and ask 'what do you think will happen next?' once.

activities.description: Teach four blocks: (i) story comprehension — characters, plot, moral; (ii) vocabulary game (match word to meaning); (iii) common vs proper nouns + adjectives, using sentences from the story; (iv) past-tense verbs (regular and irregular), with examples from the story.
teacher_actions: Walk through the four offerings; ask 'why this?' for each.
Build a table of common vs proper nouns on the board.
List 5 past-tense verbs from the story (gathered, brought, smiled, held, kept) and identify regular vs irregular.
student_actions: Pick out nouns and adjectives in sample sentences.

activities.description: Worksheet practice. Students do 5 questions: a comprehension MCQ, a vocabulary fill-blank, a noun/adjective identification, a past-tense conversion, and a short answer on the moral.
Exit-ticket: 4 quick questions covering each block of the lesson.
Set homework — a creative-writing piece on a 'precious moment' from the student's own life.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (The Raven and the Fox).

homework: Write a paragraph (4-5 sentences) describing a 'precious moment' from your own life. Use at least two adjectives and at least two past-tense verbs.
Make a list of FIVE everyday moments you might be thankful for.
Find three more proper nouns from anywhere in your textbook and three common nouns; classify each.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 10-question chapter quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on 'continuing the king's story' using a creativity + grammar rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading on the precious-moment paragraph using a two-criterion rubric (clear moment + 2 adjectives + 2 past verbs).
references: NCERT Class 6 English Poorvi, Unit 1: Fables and Folk Tales — A Bottle of Dew.
